guide:
1. Write down every tool your agent will touch and what data goes in and out of each.
2. Read the documentation of each tool before you connect it: what it needs to log in, what limits it has, what format it returns.
3. Find where the data actually lives. Enterprise databases can sit on PostgreSQL, on a separate database machine, or in a cloud environment such as Azure.
4. Map how your agent will reach each system: which connection, which credentials, which permissions.
5. Give the agent the context to finish the task: the table meanings, the rules and one worked example.
6. Run one small task end to end before you build more.
Watch out: a personal project with one data source hides all of this. Do not assume the enterprise setup will behave the same way.

## Prompt to build your own
```
I am a developer starting as an AI engineer. I will build an agent that works with <my company's systems>.
List the tools and data sources it must reach: <databases, APIs, docs>.
For each one, give me a checklist: where it lives (cloud, separate machine, local), how to connect, what access I need, and which parts of its documentation I must read first.
Then draw a simple map of how the agent reaches each system, and list the context the agent needs to finish <the task>: definitions, rules, one worked example.
Return: the checklist per system, the map as a text diagram, and the context file as markdown. Keep each part short.
```
